newsitem.title: UK: UK court to decide on Friday on tobacco case. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UK court to decide on Friday on tobacco case. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]

text.p: A British court will decide on Friday whether to appoint a judge to hear a case which could lead to massive compensation payments by British tobacco companies.

Martyn Day, lawyer for 47 lung cancer victims who have joined forces in demanding compensation from Britain's two biggest tobacco companies, said on Tuesday: "The decision has been deferred until Friday."

Day was speaking to reporters after a hearing at which the High Court was asked to name a judge to hear claims that the companies, Imperial Tobacco Group Plc and Gallaher, a former unit of American Brands Inc, which has now changed its name to Fortune Brands, had wilfully harmed their customers. (Corrects to make status of Gallaher clear.)

The British action follows a landmark tobacco settlement in the United States last month under which U.S. cigarette companies agreed to pay $385 billion over 25 years into a trust fund for people with smoking-related diseases.
Day, who is operating on a no win, no fee basis, says British tobacco companies should have known more than 40 years ago that their products were lethal but failed to minimise the risk.
Some British health authorities have also said they are considering taking legal action against the cigarette companies.
